notes: Access: robots.txt (User-agent: *) is Allow: / with only cart/checkout/query-param disallows -- no Claude-specific disallow, no policy_opt_out. Tier-1 direct HTTP (curl) worked for every real page (homepage and all category pages returned HTTP 200 with full Next.js SSR __NEXT_DATA__ JSON); no escalation to Playwright/Claude-in-Chrome needed. Site is a Next.js/React storefront (Country Road Group / David Jones-adjacent 'CRG' platform) whose SSR payload embeds a complete, structured CategoryNavigation JSON tree per page (crgApi.queries['getProductListInitialData(...)'].data.CategoryNavigation) plus an authoritative product-count field (crgApi.queries['getProductLanding-<categoryId>'].data.ProductLanding.totalCount) -- this structured data was used in preference to any displayed text, per the qty-method priority order. Discovery: fetched the top-level 'Home' department root (/home-new-in/ -> full Home category tree, categoryId 5712) and enumerated all branches (New In, New Brands, Our Edits, Our Editorials, Bathroom, Bedroom, Rugs, Kitchen & Dining, Kids Home, Home Accessories, Outdoor, Beach Towels & Accessories, Pet, Scent, Seasonal Events) down to every leaf sub-category -- none is named for or tied to a specific holiday/festival except the generic 'Seasonal Events' branch (see below). Also fetched the top-level 'Gifting' department tree (/gifting/, categoryId 150280) since this fashion+homewares retailer runs occasion-based gifting hubs outside the Home nav proper; found a live 'Father's Day' occasion node (Australian Father's Day is the first Sunday of September -- falls exactly in-season as of this check, 2026-09-04) with a Home-department-scoped child 'For The Home'. Verified the site's internal search is NOT usable as evidence: /search/?q=christmas, ?q=diwali, ?q=halloween, ?q=easter, ?q=valentine all returned near-identical non-discriminating totals (totalCount 986/1000/993/754/729) and a control query for a nonsense string (?q=zzzzznonsensequery123) also returned totalCount 1000 with an undefined first result -- confirming the search endpoint returns default/fallback results for any query and cannot prove presence or absence (matches the documented false-positive/false-absence search trap). Direct-slug probes for /christmas/, /gifting/christmas/, /diwali/, /halloween/, /valentines-day/, /easter/, /new-year/, /eid/ all returned genuine HTTP 404 (verified with full response headers, X-Next-Error-Status: 404, ruling out a transient block) -- no dedicated Christmas/Diwali/Halloween/Valentine's/Easter/New Year/Eid category or microsite currently exists on this AU storefront (plausibly pre-season; Christmas is ~3.5 months out in the Southern Hemisphere). /sitemap.xml returned a Cloudflare interactive-challenge page (tier-1 blocked for that one resource specifically) but this was not needed since the structured CategoryNavigation JSON already gave complete, non-truncated department taxonomy. INCLUDED: Father's Day > For The Home (66 products: Vara Oil Pourers, Parker Waffle Towels, Viola/Blaire glassware, Dover dinnerware, etc.) -- genuine PLP at its own URL, nested Gifting > Father's Day > For The Home in the site's own breadcrumb/pageNavigation, explicitly tied to a named occasion (Father's Day is in this project's 'Other genuine seasonal events' vocabulary), and scoped to homewares products specifically (satisfies the fashion+homewares-retailer 'scope to Home department' instruction) even though its parent 'Father's Day' hub also has non-Home children (Most Loved, Gifts under $50/$100, New Seasonal Arrivals -- these mix fashion+home and were left out of scope; Father's Day Gift Guide excluded outright as an editorial/gift-guide page per rule 17). No separate 'Father's Day' parent grouping row was added since only this one Home-scoped child was captured, not the full occasion tree. FLAGGED FOR MANUAL REVIEW (included, not silently dropped): Home > Seasonal Events > Boxed Gifts (13 products, e.g. Silk Linen Pillowcase, generic homewares) -- 'Seasonal Events' is the site's own branch name but its own banner copy ('These gifts are perfect for celebrate holidays... last minute gifts') and the child page's copy ('Beautifully packaged and ready to gift, we've hand picked a selection of our favourite homewares and wrapped them for you') never name Christmas, Diwali, or any specific occasion -- this is the recurring generic-seasonal-label pattern (rules SS5/SS6: seasonal product type/loose seasonal wording != seasonal category) seen elsewhere in this project (Westwing Fall/Spring/Summer Cushions, IKEA DE, Casa Viva, etc.); kept as a flagged row rather than silently excluded per the project's established convention for this exact ambiguity, needs a human call on whether a catalog-name-only 'Seasonal Events' branch with no named occasion qualifies. Confirmed NO_SEASONAL for: Christmas, Halloween, Diwali, Easter, Valentine's Day, Thanksgiving, New Year, Eid, Holi, and all other named holidays in the project vocabulary -- checked via (1) full structured Home-department category tree (all branches enumerated to leaf level), (2) full structured Gifting-department category tree, (3) direct URL-slug probes for every major holiday (genuine 404s, not blocks), (4) internal search proven non-discriminating so not relied on for absence. Scope: this is a fashion+homewares retailer: only Home-department-relevant categories/products were evaluated; fashion-only occasion gifting (Gifts for Her/Him/Teen, Personalised Gifts for people, etc.) was out of scope and not extracted. ADJUDICATION (2026-09-04): removed 'Seasonal Events > Boxed Gifts' row -- neither the branch's own banner copy nor the product content (Silk Linen Pillowcase and other generic pre-wrapped homewares) names or shows any specific holiday/festival, so it fails rules SS2/SS5-SS6 as a generic year-round gifting catalog reused under a loosely-seasonal branch name, not a genuine seasonal/holiday category.
